```sql
WITH gefilterde_regels AS (
    SELECT ol.variant_id::uuid AS variant_id,
           ol.order_id,
           ol.quantity,
           ol.line_total_cents
      FROM orders o
      JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_id = o.id
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       count(DISTINCT gr.order_id)  AS order_count,
       sum(gr.quantity)             AS quantity,
       sum(gr.line_total_cents)     AS revenue_cents,
       count(DISTINCT pv.id)        AS variant_count
  FROM gefilterde_regels gr
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = gr.variant_id
  JOIN products p          ON p.id = pv.product_id
 GROUP BY p.id, p.sku, p.name, p.brand, p.currency
 ORDER BY quantity DESC, revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De orderfilter wordt eerst toegepast, zodat de cast en de joins alleen op de relevante orderregels draaien. Het resultaat blijft gelijk: dezelfde aggregaten, kolommen en ORDER BY. Of de winst groot is, hangt af van de indexen en de selectiviteit van de tenant- en datumfilter, dus controleer dit met EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
